AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 7, 2019
STUDY SESSION MEETING
5:00 P.M.

REGULAR MEETING
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios
 ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR -
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez; regarding negotiations with the Norwalk
  Association of Management Employees.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54957: PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE
  EVALUATION; City Attorney.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  Pastor Ronald Spence
  Faith Church of Norwalk

FLAG SALUTE
  Olivia Morales, 5th grade
  Studebaker Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize Hometown Heroes from the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to recognize the 50th Anniversary of Municipal Clerks Week in the City of Norwalk from
  May 5 - 11, 2019.

  III.  City Council to recognize National Public Works Week from May 19 – 25, 2019.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  Egg-Stravagant Egg Hunt Celebration

  2.  6th Annual Arbor Day

  3.  Illegal Fireworks Campaign

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.
 1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of April 16,
  2019. 825-04

  Minutes

2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period March 24 – April 6, 2019,
  in the total amount of $936,658.36. 630

  Report

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period April
  10, through April 30, 2019 in the total amount of $4,268,152.40. 640

  Report

4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Roberto
  Barajas and Jerry Patterson. 830-02/16

  Report

5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS - APRIL 24, 2019 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Synopsis

6.  AGREEMENT - MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEM SERVICES - Staff recommends City
  Council approve an agreement with Knight Communications for five years from July 1, 2019 through
  June 30, 2024, in the amount of $242,782 for the first year with increases equivalent to CPI for years
  two through five; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any extensions or
  amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney. 634-04

  Report

7.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 2 – DEVELOPMENT AND CONSTRUCTION SERVICES – Staff
  recommends City Council approve an Amendment No. 2 with Terra Realty Advisors, Inc. to provide
  development and construction services for digital billboards in the amount of $18,000; and authorize
  the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 2 and any additional amendments provided there is
  funding in budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 925-13

  Report

8.  PROJECT NO. 7357 - INSTALLATION OF CHAIN LINK FENCING ON ACQUIRED TANK FARM
  PROPERTY ADJACENT TO HOLIFIELD PARK, ENGINEERS REPORT NO. 19-09 – Staff
  recommends City Council award a contract to Alcorn Fence Company of Sun Valley in the amount of
  $46,514 for the installation of chain link fencing on acquired Tank Farm property adjacent to Holifield
  Park; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided there
  is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7357

  Report

9.  ACCEPTANCE OF WORK FOR REPLACEMENT OF AIR-COOLED CHILLER FOR CITY HALL
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS – Staff recommends City Council accept the work of ACCO Engineered
  Systems, Inc. in the amount of $97,781 for removal and replacement of the existing 50-ton, air-cooled
  chiller for the City Hall Council Chambers. 920-01-04

  Report

10. ENVIRONMENTAL ENHANCEMENT AND MITIGATION PROGRAM (EEMP) GRANT WRITING
  SERVICES FOR REMOVAL OF TURF AND INSTALLATION OF DROUGHT TOLERANT PLANTS IN
  MEDIANS – Staff recommends City Council authorize the use of Greenscape funds in the amount of
  $8,990 for grant writing services to apply for the 2019 EEMP grant.
   Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

  12. PRIVATE SECTOR REPRESENTATIVE FOR THE SOUTHEAST LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT BOARD – Staff recommends City Council reappoint Mr. Joseph
  Derthick as the City of Norwalk’s private sector representative for another two-year term ending June
  30, 2021. 135-15-01

  Report

  13. FISCAL AND DEVELOPMENT AD HOC COMMITTEE APPOINTMENTS – Staff recommends City
  Council select two members to serve on each of the Fiscal and Development Ad Hoc Committees.

  Report

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  14. CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING - APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S DENIAL OF
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 1006 AND PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2001 -
  PROPOSED RECYCLING CENTER AT 11018-11030 ROSECRANS AVENUE - Staff recommends City
  Council direct staff as deemed appropriate. 320-01-1006/320-04-2001

  Report

  15. CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING – APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S REVOCATION OF
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 934 AND ZONE VARIANCE NO. 333 - JAYNESHWAR GOUNDER,
  DHAKA LIQUOR AND MARKET, 10944 IMPERIAL HIGHWAY – Staff recommends City Council direct
  staff as deemed appropriate. 320-01-934/320-11-333

  Report

CALL TO ORDER THE NORWALK COMMUNITY FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY

  16. STREET IMPROVEMENTS FINANCING – RESOLUTION NO. 19-22 AND NORWALK COMMUNITY
  FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY RESOLUTION NO. NCFFA-22 – Staff recommends:

  a.  City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-22, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF NORWALK APPROVING THE ISSUANCE OF BONDS BY THE NORWALK COMMUNITY
  FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY TO FINANCE MEASURE M AND MEASURE R
  (TRANSPORTATION) PROJECTS, THE CITY’S EXECUTION OF PLEDGE AGREEMENTS, AND
  AUTHORIZING AND DIRECTING CERTAIN ACTIONS WITH RESPECT THERETO; and

  b.  the Norwalk Community Facilities Financing Authority adopt Resolution No. NCFFA-22, A
  RESOLUTION OF NORWALK COMMUNITY FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY
  AUTHORIZING THE ISSUANCE AND SALE OF NOT TO EXCEED $25,000,000 AGGREGATE
  PRINCIPAL AMOUNT OF NORWALK COMMUNITY FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY
  SALES TAX REVENUE BONDS (LIMITED TAX BONDS) (MEASURE M), SERIES 2019A AND
  NORWALK COMMUNITY FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY SALES TAX REVENUE BONDS
  (LIMITED TAX BONDS) (MEASURE R), SERIES 2019B, APPROVAL OF INDENTURES AND
  PLEDGE AGREEMENTS AND AUTHORIZING ACTIONS AND EXECUTION OF DOCUMENTS
  RELATED THERETO. 620-02-17
  ADJOURN THE NORWALK COMMUNITY FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY

  Report

PUBLIC HEARINGS – CONTINUED
   17. RESOLUTION NO. 19-21 – THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME FISCAL
  YEAR 2019/20 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN, MINORITY & WOMEN-OWNED BUSINESSES POLICIES
  AND PROCEDURES, HOME PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 19-21, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME
  FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN, MINORITY & WOMEN-OWNED BUSINESSES
  POLICIES AND PROCEDURES, HOME PROGRAM: HOMEBUYER MANUAL, AN APPLICATION
  FOR CDBG AND HOME FUNDING FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY
  MANAGER TO EXECUTE AND TRANSMIT ALL REQUIRED DOCUMENTS TO THE UNITED
  STATES DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT;

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute agreements and any amendments, in a form approved by
  the City Attorney with social service agencies for the provision of services funded under the Annual
  Action Plan; and

  c.  authorize the Director of Community Development to execute a Memorandum of Understanding
  with City Departments and homeless referral organizations for the provision of services funded
  under the Annual Action Plan. 315

  Report

  18. RESOLUTION NO. 19-18 – APPROVING SPECIAL REGULATORY PROVISIONS FOR SMALL
  WIRELESS FACILITIES PURSUANT TO NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 17.02.295.A AND
  17.02.295.B AND THE REPORT AND ORDER AND DECLARATORY RULING ADOPTED BY THE
  UNITED STATES FEDERAL COMMUNICATIONS COMMISSION ON SEPTEMBER 26, 2018;
  RESOLUTION NO. 19-19 - ADOPTING CERTAIN SMALL CELL WIRELESS AND WIRELESS
  COLLOCATION PERMIT APPLICATION FEES; AND RESOLUTION NO. 19-20 - ADOPTING A POLE
  LICENSE AGREEMENT AND ASSOCIATED FEES FOR INSTALLATION OF A NEW SMALL
  WIRELESS FACILITY ON CITY-OWNED INFRASTRUCTURE – Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 19-18, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPROVING SPECIAL REGULATORY PROVISIONS FOR SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES
  PURSUANT TO NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 17.02.295.A AND 17.02.295.B AND
  THE REPORT AND ORDER AND DECLARATORY RULING ADOPTED BY THE UNITED STATES
  FEDERAL COMMUNICATIONS COMMISSION ON SEPTEMBER 26, 2018;

  b.  Resolution No. 19-19, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  SETTING FORTH ITS FINDINGS OF FACT AND DECISION RELATIVE TO THE
  ESTABLISHMENT OF COST-RECOVERY, REGULATORY SMALL CELL WIRELESS AND
  WIRELESS COLLOCATION PERMIT APPLICATION FEES TO THE CITY’S COMPREHENSIVE
  FEE SCHEDULE; and

  c.  Resolution No. 19-20, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPROVING THE FORM AND MATERIAL TERMS OF A POLE LICENSE AGREEMENT FOR
  WIRELESS FACILITIES AND RELATED REASONABLE, COST-RECOVERY FEES. 1060-09

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated May 2, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
